title: Invisible Burden of Chronic Inflammatory Skin Disease
summary:
Chronic inflammatory skin diseases such as atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, or hidradenitis suppurativa can place a considerable burden on everyday life. The symptoms do not affect the skin alone. Many people need to organise regular medical appointments, carry out treatments, or repeatedly deal with issues related to their condition. Some frequently worry about how the disease may develop or search for information online. The time and energy required to manage the condition in daily life can also be burdensome.

To date, studies have mainly focused on visible skin changes and quality of life. By contrast, the many organisational, time-related, and emotional burdens associated with managing the disease have rarely been investigated. It is therefore not yet sufficiently understood how strongly these “invisible” burdens affect the daily lives of people with chronic inflammatory skin diseases.

The aim of this study is to gain a better understanding of these previously under-recognised effects. The findings are intended to help identify the needs of people with chronic inflammatory skin diseases more effectively and to further improve medical care in the future.

interventions.name: Patients with chronic inflammatory skin diseases who are not starting a new systemic therapy complete a paper-based questionnaire once at study enrolment.
Patients with chronic inflammatory skin diseases who start a new systemic therapy complete the questionnaire at study enrolment and again after 3 and 6 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Diagnosis of a chronic inflammatory skin disease, such as psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, or hidradenitis suppurativa
•	Sufficient proficiency in German to complete the questionnaires
•	Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
•	Age below 18 years or above 65 years
